item.title: US officials recover audio from ‘Mississippi miracle’ cruise ship and tanker crash
item.description:
Thirty-two people are in local hospitals and all passengers and crew are accounted for after a tanker collided with a Mississippi River cruise ship near the Port of New Orleans , officials said Friday. The big picture: With approximately 180 people on the ship, the rescue of all aboard is "truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said at a press conference. What they're saying: While the investigation remains ongoing, officials said the Atlantic Asphalt tanker appeared to have lost control, causing it to collide with the cruise ship. As passengers were disembarking after the collision, the cruise ship began to sink and eventually toppled over and flipped — leaving people in the cold water. item.title: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
item.description:
Authorities say Russian intelligence service ordered attack which Estonian PM links to Tallinn’s support for Ukraine Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after a suspected sabotage attack on a drone maker in the Baltic state over the weekend, which authorities said was ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence service. On Saturday morning, eight people were detained during an attempted attack on Threod Systems, a defence company that manufactures long-range attack and reconnaissance drones. No injuries or damage were reported after the company’s security team responded to the incident. Continue reading...

item.title: Yemen: Anti-Houthi forces pull back as rebels advance

item.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
item.description:
Throughout Israel’s war on Palestine, doctors Thaer Ahmad and Feroze Sidhwa spent months at Nasser Hospital in the southern Gaza city of Khan Younis, where they provided care as volunteers and survived a raid and an airstrike on the complex. item.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit – video
item.description:
SpaceX made history by catching the upper stage of the largest and most powerful rocket ever built as a pivotal step for the company in its aim to create the first fully reusable rocket. Starship Flight 15, which launched at 5:47 p.m. ET Friday from Starbase in South Texas, achieved the monumental feat of catching the upper stage — called Starship, or “Ship” — of the rocket using the launch tower’s “chopstick” arms on its return to Earth at 4:20 p.m. ET Saturday. item.title: ‘The blood of these brothers cries out’: Pope Leo demands justice for people killed protecting the Amazon
item.description:
Pontiff delivers forceful speech on final day in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining. On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation. item.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu can’t remain Israel PM amid alleged vote meddling
item.description:
Prime ministerial hopeful calls Arab minority ‘an integral part of the Israeli story’ as he seeks to form government Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot condemned a “racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation” against the country’s Arab citizens, after the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, accused Arab parties of electoral fraud without evidence. Netanyahu has repeatedly targeted Arab parties and Palestinian citizens of Israel after his party received a disappointing electoral showing, accusing them of manipulating the election and being linked to Hamas. Israeli electoral authorities have rejected these claims as not being backed by evidence. Continue reading...

item.title: Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies age 80
item.description:
Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in hospital on Sunday aged 80 after suffering multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. Imprisoned since 1989, he had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.
